review_method: Analyst-assisted examination of actual Reuters reporting and an original BLS release; this is not an autonomous verification run.
report_headline: US producer prices post largest gain in 4-1/2 years; expensive gasoline boosts retail sales

findings.claim: The final-demand Producer Price Index increased 1.3 percent in September 2026, seasonally adjusted.
findings.source_evidence: The Producer Price Index for final demand increased 1.3 percent in September, seasonally adjusted
findings.reason: BLS explicitly reports the figure, period, metric and adjustment.

findings.claim: It was the largest monthly producer-price rise in about four and a half years.
findings.source_evidence: The September increase is the largest advance since rising 1.7 percent in March 2022
findings.reason: March 2022 to September 2026 is approximately 4.5 years.

findings.claim: Final-demand producer prices rose 6.3 percent over 12 months.
findings.source_evidence: the index for final demand climbed 6.3 percent for the 12 months ended in September
findings.reason: BLS explicitly reports the unadjusted year-over-year change.

findings.claim: The producer-price increase proves consumers' prices increased by an identical amount.
findings.source_evidence: PPIs measure price change from the perspective of the seller.
findings.reason: The PPI is not the CPI. No fixed one-to-one consumer pass-through is established.

scope_limitations: Verified status applies to specific BLS figures, not every interpretation or forward-looking statement in the Reuters article.
Source excerpts were compared by an analyst, not by a fully autonomous semantic verification service.
The provided Reuters item is a news source, while BLS is the competent authority for its published PPI series.
